resources.string: This MVP is not ready for real sensitive conversations. Its simplified session layer and experimental components require independent security review.
No phone number and no address book upload. A cryptographic identity will be created only for this device.
There are no contacts yet. Add a contact using a QR invitation.
Share this QR code only with the person you intend to contact.
For two-way conversation, exchange two invitations: A shows a QR code and B scans it, then B shows a QR code and A scans it. Importing an invitation does not automatically trust a device.
Ready means this device has a usable receiving address for the contact. Replies require the contact to import your invitation separately.
For a two-way conversation, the second phone must also show its QR code and the first phone must scan it.
For a two-way conversation, the other user must also import your invitation. Unknown contacts are not created automatically.
Scan a secure invitation QR code
Enter a contact name before importing the invitation.
Paste or scan an invitation code before import.
The invitation code is corrupted or invalid.
This invitation version is not supported by this build.
Contact added. Verify the safety number before important messages.
New device recorded as pending approval. Delivery to it is not enabled.
This prototype cannot open the stored session. Re-verification is required before sending.
Delivery is blocked because the receiving device is not approved or its security state changed. Review it in Contact Security.
Relay synchronization was requested. Retryable failed messages will be attempted now when the network is available.
Paranoia C4 mode is experimental in this version. Do not use this application for real sensitive conversations until an independent audit has been completed.
Unavailable in this build: audited primitive implementations and test vectors are required.
This contact is unverified. Before sending important messages, compare the safety number or perform QR verification.
This contact\'s security key has changed. This may indicate a new device, an app reinstall, or an attempted attack. Verify the contact again.
Scan the contact verification QR code
The scanned verification code does not match this contact. Do not mark the device as verified.
Compare this number in person or using a trusted channel, then mark the device as verified.
New device detected. Verify its safety number through a trusted channel before approving it. Messages are not sent to this device automatically.
A contact device has been revoked. Encrypted delivery to that device is blocked until it is explicitly verified again.
Paste a separate invitation received from this contact. A new device remains inactive until you verify it.
Development delivery endpoint for this device. For a physical phone on the same Wi-Fi network, enter the laptop LAN address.
Emulator LAN default: http://10.0.2.2:8787. Physical LAN example: http://192.168.1.45:8787. Public tunnel example: https://example-relay.example.
HTTP relay is permitted only in this debug build for local Wi-Fi testing. It does not protect network metadata or transport integrity.
Insecure HTTP relay is blocked in release builds. Enter an HTTPS relay URL.
On a physical phone, 127.0.0.1 and localhost point to the phone itself, not your laptop. Use the laptop Wi-Fi address, for example http://192.168.0.87:8787.
0.0.0.0 is valid for a server listening on all interfaces, but it is not a client address. On a physical phone, use the laptop Wi-Fi address, for example http://192.168.0.87:8787.
Public relay / tunnel mode uses an HTTPS URL that both the phone and emulator can reach.
HTTP is allowed only for debug LAN testing.
For tests across different networks, use an HTTPS relay URL.
Background synchronization is best effort and may be delayed by Android power management.
Save the Relay URL first, open the conversation being tested, and run this check before sending.
For a physical phone, specify the laptop IP address rather than 127.0.0.1 or localhost.
For a physical phone, specify the laptop IP address rather than 0.0.0.0.
Sending is blocked by the device state.
There are messages awaiting another delivery attempt.
Placeholder: biometric or PIN unlock is not implemented in this MVP.
This action deletes local messages, contacts, and keys from this device. The data cannot be recovered.
Debug-only test reset deletes the local profile, contacts, messages, sessions, retry/replay state, disabled Signal spike records and diagnostics. The saved Relay URL is kept for repeated LAN testing.

This is a destructive debug action. It permanently deletes local test profiles, messages, contacts, cryptographic state, pending delivery and diagnostic history from this device. The saved Relay URL remains. Continue only when you intend to restart the test.
Diagnostics export is a placeholder. No message text, private keys, session keys, nonces, or decrypted files may be exported.
This technical report contains statuses, counts, timestamps, and short identifier fingerprints only. It excludes message text, keys, nonces, and ciphertext.
Sending is blocked by the device state
Sending is blocked: no primary contact device is available.
Sending is blocked: the primary device is pending approval.
Sending is blocked: the primary device has been revoked.
Sending is blocked: the primary device key has changed.
Development relay delivery is active when a local relay server is running. The relay receives encrypted blobs only.
